claims.text: Under conventional moderate cooling, molten Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
Moderate cooling produces limited amorphous retention in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Melt-spinning can provide the extremely rapid cooling required by the proposed intervention.
A cooling rate exceeding approximately 10^5 K/s is required to suppress primary crystallization in this alloy.
Cooling above approximately 10^5 K/s will suppress primary crystallization in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 relative to slower cooling.
Extremely rapid cooling inhibits atomic diffusion needed for crystal nucleation.
Reduced atomic mobility leaves insufficient time for the nucleation and growth of multiple crystalline phases.
Suppressing nucleation and crystal growth enables formation of a metastable amorphous structure.
Kinetic suppression of crystallization promotes glass formation in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Kinetic suppression of crystallization increases the thermal stability of the resulting amorphous phase.
Melt-spinning above the proposed cooling-rate threshold will produce a higher retained amorphous fraction than slower cooling.
Melt-spinning above the proposed cooling-rate threshold will increase the crystallization-onset temperature during subsequent reheating relative to slower-cooled samples.
Keeping subsequent reheating below approximately 0.9Tg will avoid triggering crystallization.
Cooling below the critical rate or reheating to the crystallization-initiation temperature may result in incomplete suppression of crystallization.

contradictions.description: The conditions and boundary present >10^5 K/s as a required critical threshold, while the uncertainty field states that the quantitative cooling-rate threshold is not precisely known. Calling the value approximate softens but does not eliminate this precision mismatch.

The reheating protocol is said to remain below the conventional crystallization onset, yet the experiment is also supposed to measure and compare crystallization-onset temperatures. A DSC scan must reach or cross the relevant onset to observe it directly.
